headline: Growth stays strong while acquisition costs squeeze margins
summary_short: Q2 revenue rose 24.0% y/y to $3.99B, beating the high end of guidance on every topline and profitability metric, while GAAP operating margin fell to 4.1% from 11.1% a year ago as stock-based compensation, acquisition-related intangible amortization, and business-combination costs climbed sharply.
summary_long: Subscription revenue (+24.5% y/y) beat the high end of guidance on net new ACV outperformance and stronger on-premise mix, aided by U.S. Federal demand. Cost of revenue grew faster (+61.5% y/y) on higher stock comp and acquisition-related intangible amortization, compressing GAAP gross margin to 70.7% and operating margin to 4.1% (non-GAAP operating margin flat at 29.5%). Net income of $298M was cushioned by a $273M unrealized gain on strategic investments and a $51M tax valuation-allowance release. Cash fell to $2.50B on $7.45B of business-combination payments, partly offset by $3.94B of new senior notes and commercial paper proceeds. FY2026 subscription revenue guidance raised to $15,760-$15,780M.

drivers.explanation: Subscription revenue beat the high end of guidance on net new ACV outperformance and stronger on-premise revenue mix, aided by U.S. Federal demand pulling some on-premise revenue forward from Q3.
Growth outpaced revenue mainly from higher stock-based compensation and a sharp rise in amortization of purchased intangibles, per the non-GAAP reconciliation table.
Cost of revenue grew 61.5% y/y against 24.0% revenue growth, compressing gross margin; the reconciliation attributes most of the gap to acquisition-related intangible amortization and stock comp.
GAAP operating margin fell to 4% from 11% as stock-based comp, intangible amortization, business-combination costs, and severance all rose; non-GAAP operating margin held flat at 29.5%.
Decline was cushioned by a $273 million unrealized gain on strategic investments and a $51 million tax valuation-allowance release, partly offsetting weaker operating income.
Mirrors the net income decline; diluted share count was roughly flat y/y, so EPS moved in line with net income.
Cash fell mainly from $7.45 billion of business-combination payments this quarter, per the cash-flow statement, partly offset by $3.94 billion of new senior notes and commercial paper proceeds.
Company beat the high end of guidance on every quarterly topline and profitability metric and raised FY2026 subscription revenue guidance on net-new-ACV strength.
